title: Connect Claude to Your Meeting Notes (Desktop & Code) | Meetily

children.text: Connect Claude to Your Meeting Notes

Meetily Pro's built-in MCP server lets Claude Desktop and Claude Code search your meetings, read transcripts and summaries and, if you allow it, start or stop a recording. Meetily records and transcribes on your own Windows or Mac computer with no meeting bot, and you connect Claude in one click from Meetily's Settings, choosing exactly what it may do.
READING IS ALWAYS ON, EVERYTHING ELSE IS OPT-IN
Last updated: September 25, 2026 • Reviewed by the Meetily team
Can Claude read my meeting notes?

Yes, once you connect it. Meetily Pro 1.11.0 includes an MCP server, the standard way Claude connects to other apps. With it, Claude can search every transcript, list your meetings, read a transcript or summary, and export a meeting. With the Record permission it can also start or stop a recording, and with Write it can edit or regenerate a summary. Meetily still does the recording and transcription on your own computer; Claude reads the results when you ask.
How do I connect Claude Desktop to Meetily?
Update to Meetily Pro 1.11.0 or later. The 14-day trial works.
Open Settings > PRO and turn on Integrations. The Integrations tab appears.
Click Connect next to Claude Desktop and choose what Claude may do. New connections start read-only.
Turn on Claude Desktop’s Allow switch.
Restart Claude Desktop so it loads the Meetily tools, then ask it about a meeting.

How do I connect Claude Code to Meetily?

The same way: when Claude Code is installed on the same computer (Meetily looks for the claude command-line tool), it appears in the Integrations tab with its own Connect button and its own permissions. Turn on its Allow switch, then start a new Claude Code session so it loads the Meetily tools. Claude Code is useful when a meeting decides something about your code, for example “read Monday’s architecture review and list the API changes we agreed.” For manual setup, follow the up-to-date guide in the meetily-workflows repository.
What can I ask Claude about my meetings?
Anything the meetings can answer. A few examples:
“What did we decide about the pricing page in Tuesday's product sync?”
“List every action item assigned to me in this week's meetings.”
“Summarize the customer calls that mentioned SSO.”
“Draft a follow-up email from yesterday's call with the Acme team.”
The last one needs the Record permission.
What does Claude see, and where does it go?

Claude sees the meetings it reads when you ask, through the permissions you chose. Meetily serves them on your own computer, but Claude then sends what it reads to Anthropic, the same as anything else you ask it. If that matters for a meeting, keep that meeting out of the conversation, or read how Anthropic handles your data first. Transcription itself always runs locally.
What if Claude does not see Meetily?

Check that the Automation API switch is on in the Integrations tab and that Claude’s Allow switch is on, then restart Claude. If it still does not work, run the built-in check in a terminal. It confirms Meetily is reachable and your Pro license is active:
Settings > PRO > Integrations. The Integrations tab appears with the Automation API switch on.
Click Connect next to Claude Desktop or Claude Code, choose what it may do, then turn on its Allow switch.
Restart Claude so it loads the Meetily tools, then ask about any meeting.

children.q: Does connecting Claude to Meetily need Meetily Pro?
children.a: Yes. The MCP server that Claude connects to is part of Meetily Pro 1.11.0 and later ($10/user/month billed annually), and it is included in the 14-day Pro trial. The free Community Edition does not include it.

children.q: Does it work with Claude on the web?
children.a: No. The Meetily MCP server runs on your own computer, so it works with Claude Desktop and Claude Code installed on the same machine. Claude in a browser cannot reach it.

No. Meetily's MCP server has no tool for deleting meetings, whatever permissions you set. A new connection starts read-only; recording and editing summaries are separate switches in the Claude panel in Meetily.

children.q: Does Anthropic get my meeting notes?
children.a: Claude sends what it reads from Meetily to Anthropic, the same as anything else you ask it, and Anthropic handles it under its own terms. Meetily transcribes and stores your meetings on your computer; Claude only sees the meetings it reads when you ask.

children.q: Claude does not show the Meetily tools. What should I check?
children.a: Check that the Automation API switch is on in the Integrations tab and that Claude's Allow switch is on, then restart Claude Desktop or your Claude Code session. Running meetily-pro mcp doctor in a terminal checks that Meetily is reachable and that your Pro license is active.

children.q: I changed Claude's permissions. Why can't it use them yet?
children.a: Claude loads the Meetily tools when it starts. After you change what Claude may do, restart Claude Desktop or your Claude Code session so it picks up the new permissions.
